review.decision: Proceed with building 100 deterministic research tests for Phoenix, adhering strictly to the specified families and constraints.
objections: Tests may not cover all edge cases in production.
Deterministic paths may not reflect real-world randomness.
Library references could introduce hidden dependencies.
No stress testing for correlated underlyings.
No testing for numerical stability in extreme scenarios.
No testing for parallel execution safety.
No testing for memory leaks in long paths.
No testing for thread safety in shared fixtures.
No testing for reproducibility across environments.
acceptance_tests: All 100 tests run without errors in a clean environment.
All tests produce deterministic outputs for the same seed.
All tests pass with pure path fixtures (no external data).
All tests pass with optional library references (if used).
No tests rely on production-side changes or configurations.
All tests pass with zero market data assumptions.
All tests pass with no OOS calculations or side effects.
All tests pass with no state mutations or external calls.
All tests pass with no hidden dependencies or side effects.
All tests pass with no numerical instability in extreme scenarios.
implementation_notes: Use pure path fixtures for all scenarios (e.g., `numpy` or `scipy` for deterministic paths).
Avoid external dependencies unless explicitly required by the test.
Ensure all tests are self-contained and do not rely on external state.
Use fixed random seeds for reproducibility (e.g., `np.random.seed(42)`).
Implement tests as independent units with no shared state.
Document all assumptions and constraints in test metadata.
Use assertions to validate deterministic outputs.
Avoid hardcoding market data; use synthetic or generated data.
Ensure all tests pass in isolation and in combination.
Log all test runs for debugging and validation.
safety_flags: No external API calls or network dependencies.
No file I/O or disk writes (unless explicitly required).
No use of global state or mutable shared resources.
No reliance on system time or non-deterministic sources.
No use of uninitialized variables or undefined behavior.
No assumptions about underlying distributions or correlations.
No use of floating-point operations that may introduce instability.
No use of parallelism unless explicitly tested for thread safety.
No use of external libraries unless explicitly allowed.
No assumptions about production environment or configurations.
